articles.body: In Argentina, a nation of meat lovers par excellence, where barbecuing is a ritual central to the national identity and the steaks are among the best in the world, meat consumption has now reached an all-time low. The reason: the drastic decline in purchasing power for most Argentines since Javier Milei took office. Our reporters explain.
articles.headline: Argentina shuns meat as purchasing plummets under Milei

articles.body: In the last ten years, South Korea has established itself as a powerhouse of beauty and cosmetics. France 24’s Christina Yoon, Mélodie Sforza and Jan Camezind Broomby sent this report from Seoul.
articles.headline: 'A face lift once a month': Growing pressure to conform amid the rise of Korea's 'K-Beauty'

articles.body: Benjamin Netanyahu travelled secretly to the United Arab Emirates over the weekend, Israeli media has reported, to ask its leader to deny claims he had warned the Israeli prime minister about a looming Hamas threat ahead of the Palestinian militant group's Oct. 7, 2023 attack on southern Israel. articles.headline: Was Netanyahu warned of October 7 Hamas attacks?

articles.body: The king of Morocco on Tuesday named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri the country's first woman prime minister after her centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) party won last week's parliamentary elections. El Mansouri joined the PAM in 2008 and was also the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh, winning the office in 2009 before losing it six years later, then retaking it again in 2021.
articles.headline: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri named Morocco's first woman PM

articles.body: Ethiopia has one of the oldest Jewish communities in the world, rumoured to be the descendants of the Queen of Sheba and King Solomon in 950 BC. articles.body: Sen. Jon Ossoff hosted a few hundred donors and supporters for a recent Washington fundraiser — but it wasn’t just for him. Instead, the Sept. 16 gathering was geared toward raising money for the Democratic Party of Georgia and its coordinated campaign, according to an Ossoff aide and one attendee, who was granted anonymity to describe a private event. It's part of his broader effort to boost state Democrats as they look to flip the governor’s mansion for the first time in over 20 years and improve their margins in the legislature. And the timing, just weeks before November, signals confidence in Ossoff’s own reelection prospects and the sizable warchest he’s raised for himself . This month’s event was the latest of several similar fundraisers Ossoff has held over the last two years. He plans to host more fundraisers for Georgia’s Democratic Party and the coordinated campaign ahead of Election Day, according to one person familiar with his planning, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly. If his moves are successful and November ushers in historic wins for Georgia Democrats, Ossoff will have cemented his status as a serious leader in the critical swing state. He would hold on to a crucial seat in the Senate as the party looks toward the South to shore up its future. He’d be credited in part with helping elect former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms as the country’s first Black woman governor. And though Ossoff has said he’s not interested in joining a 2028 presidential race, leading a November sweep would ultimately raise his national profile. “It would be hard to call him anything but a leader of the [state] party at that point. He's already inching his way towards that kind of designation,” said Andrew Heaton, a Georgia-based Democratic strategist who supports the ticket. “But if there is the kind of success that a lot of people are predicting for the cycle, he would receive a large portion of the credit for that.” Ossoff’s campaign did not comment beyond confirming the fundraisers. The events are just part of Ossoff’s endeavor to help build out the Georgia Democratic Party’s apparatus after a rough 2024 election cycle. The senator has transferred $3.6 million of his own campaign funds to the party’s coordinated campaign to date, which the Atlanta Journal-Constitution first reported . Since the effort was announced in July, the party has opened 30 field offices across the sizable state, and employs more than 100 field staffers helping with grassroots organizing for races up and down the ballot. The coordinated campaign is led by a former Ossoff political director, Kyle Tromley. Caroline Saudek, a longtime fundraiser for Ossoff’s political operation, also joined the state party in January in a fundraising-focused role. Democrats across the state — from the densely populated Atlanta metro to Georgia’s small sliver of Atlantic coast — said they’ve seen a marked difference in the coordinated campaign’s involvement this cycle, from consistent communication to investment in smaller-profile races. That transformation, several noted, started when Chair Charlie Bailey took the helm. Bailey, an attorney from rural Harris County and former statewide candidate for lieutenant governor, became the leader of the party in mid-2025 with Ossoff’s crucial support . “It is definitely a stronger coordinated campaign than I've seen in years, and in previous cycles. And it feels like it is better staffed, they staffed up earlier,” Heaton, the Georgia-based Democratic strategist, said. Republicans are also taking note of the newly improved Democratic machine in a state that, until 2020, was a safe-red hold for the most high-profile races. Already, GOP fears are growing about Rep. Mike Collins’ ability to beat Ossoff . And polls show GOP gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson locked in a tight battle with Bottoms, despite having dropped tens of millions from his own bank account into the race. Georgia Republican Party Chair Josh McKoon shrugged off Democrats’ fundraising efforts and said he feels “very good” about Republicans’ field resources. “We've had a field program in place for months now. We have field staff on the ground all over the state,” he said in an interview, though he declined to provide details on the size of the Georgia GOP’s paid and volunteer operation. Others aren’t as dismissive. “The Democratic Party has deployed resources to hire staff that mobilizes and turns out voters. Republicans have not had this competitive of a race in a while, so they don’t have that type of muscle memory,” said Ryan Mahoney, a longtime Georgia-based Republican strategist. “The Democrats are in such a great spot,” he added. “It's because the apparatus has been tested and is working.”
articles.headline: Jon Ossoff’s hosting fundraisers — and they’re not all for his reelection campaign

articles.body: Facing his toughest election challenge in years, GOP Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick has blanketed southeast Pennsylvania with attacks on his Democratic opponent — many of them citing what appear to be independent local news reports. “Bob Harvie calls himself a king,” reads one article quoted in a June television spot . “Bob Harvie has his FBI files but refuses to release them,” reads another headline quoted in a September digital ad . Another quotes , “Bob Harvie to independent voters: ‘join a political party or lose your right to vote.’” These ads and five others all cite headlines from Patch, once a well-funded experiment in “hyperlocal” news that garnered hefty audiences in some communities but has since withered into a largely unedited volunteer operation. That isn’t the only reason to question the reliability of coverage referenced in the ads: Each of the articles cited carry the byline of Dave Sommers, a Levittown, Pennsylvania, man with close ties to Fitzpatrick and a checkered history with law enforcement. The battle for the 1st Congressional District has grown increasingly nasty as the five-term incumbent battles national headwinds for Republicans and tries to fend off a spirited challenge from Harvie, a Bucks County commissioner. Central to the GOP defense strategy has been a costly ad blitz, with Fitzpatrick and allies trying to paint Harvie not as a devoted public servant but as an ethically compromised political operator — using Sommers’ headlines as key fodder. Sommers has received sporadic payments and reimbursements from Fitzpatrick’s campaign, as well as from the campaign of his late brother, Republican Rep. Mike Fitzpatrick, dating back to 2010. As recently as 2022, Brian Fitzpatrick’s campaign paid Sommers $500 for “office setup services,” according to Federal Election Commission records. That year, Sommers was charged with stealing an election sign that expressed support for a GOP primary challenger, Alex Entin, according to a local news report . Sommers has been pictured with Fitzpatrick at campaign and personal events. Fitzpatrick’s Facebook page shows Sommers posing next to the lawmaker at a March 2025 St. Patrick's Day parade. Sommers' own Facebook has featured a stream of posts supporting Fitzpatrick, including one post from June where Sommers is seen sporting a tank top with the phrase “Team Fitz.” Sommers also attended Fitzpatrick's June wedding, according to multiple social media posts. In one wedding photo posted to Sommers’ Facebook , he poses with former Sen. Joe Manchin (I-W.Va.), also a guest. Sommers did not respond to repeated requests for comment about his relationship to Fitzpatrick and his campaign. Spokespeople for the Fitzpatrick campaign also did not respond to multiple requests for comment. Reilly Richardson, a spokesperson for the House GOP campaign arm, pointed in a statement to a Friday report that Harvie passed off “known Democrat activists” as “concerned voters” in his own ads and accused him of “lying to voters.” “Now, he’s desperately trying to distract from his pathetic, flailing campaign, but Pennsylvanians won’t be fooled,” Richardson said of Harvie. Sommers is a retired reporter who worked for the Bucks County Courier Times, the Trentonian and other local outlets. He drew headlines of his own after he was prosecuted for trafficking in protected turtles . Prosecutors alleged he made more than $500,000 over six years selling diamondback terrapins online, running afoul of state and federal conservation laws . Sommers was handed a six-month prison sentence in 2019, along with six months of house arrest and a $250,000 fine. Sommers opened a more recent chapter as a Patch contributor, posting eight articles dating back to late February. They all attack Harvie, slamming him for being “divisive,” “arrogant” and a “hack.” They feature messaging consistent with the Fitzpatrick campaign, including an Aug. 27 post which accuses Harvie of wanting “more data centers in Bucks County.” Harvie in a statement called Fitzpatrick “a complete and total fraud” and said he’s growing “desperate.” “Brian Fitzpatrick is worse than the rest of the Washington swamp because he pretends to be different, but the receipts show he is corrupt to the core,” he said. Harvie has also repeatedly denied several of the Fitzpatrick campaign and its allies’ characterizations of his record, particularly that he was the target of any FBI investigation. Harvie testified before a federal grand jury with other officials in September 2022 as part of an apparent public corruption probe, according to a local report . He sent a cease-and-desist letter to Fitzpatrick in July, claiming defamation in campaign ads. He also sued the pro-Fitzpatrick Defending America PAC in August for defamatory statements. The use of headlines mined from self-publishing platforms in political ads is not unheard of, with outlets such as Medium and Substack offering opportunities for both parties to pass off politically motivated attacks as independent reporting. Campaigns around the country have drawn scrutiny for leaning on articles in their campaign materials from partisan sources or that misrepresent their origin — but rarely are they citing sources that have such direct ties to the candidate. Posting on Patch, like those other platforms, requires only creating an account. An email associated with Sommers appears to be tied to a Patch account, prompting a “Welcome back!” message when it is used to try to open a new account.
articles.headline: Brian Fitzpatrick’s campaign ads feature damning news headlines. They're not from an unbiased source.

articles.body: POLICING PROBLEMS: In the early days of his administration, Mayor Zohran Mamdani placed a new requirement on the NYPD: The department would have to secure permission from his office to deploy its Strategic Response Group to make arrests at protests. The directive, which hasn’t been previously reported, shows Mamdani sought to exert significant influence over a core function of the police department. Its existence also calls into question why the mayor hasn’t more frequently used that authority to stop the SRG from being deployed at protests — since he promised as a candidate to disband the specialized unit. The unit — which has long weathered criticism for its heavy-handed protest responses — just last week arrested activists protesting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s appearance at the United Nations General Assembly. Several politicians allied with Mamdani were among those put in handcuffs. When asked about those arrests, an NYPD spokesperson revealed the pre-approval policy to Playbook, confirming that the mayor’s office has the final say whenever the department wants to deploy SRG to detain protesters. “We communicate with City Hall on this topic as we do on a host of things related to the department,” the spokesperson said. The police spokesperson declined to comment on when exactly the mayor first instituted the SRG pre-clearance process. But a person familiar with the timing, who was granted anonymity to discuss the sensitive issue, said the policy was put in place during the first few months of Mamdani’s term. The mayor suggested at a press conference on Monday that he didn’t see a justification for using the SRG in last week’s arrests outside the U.N. “I’ve been clear that my vision is for the disbanding of the SRG,” he told reporters when asked if he thought it was an appropriate use of police resources. A Mamdani spokesperson declined to comment Tuesday on why the mayor didn’t use his power to call back the SRG last week if he didn’t think its deployment was justified. The spokesperson also would not say if the mayor has ever used his authority to reject a request from the NYPD for SRG intervention. Amanda Jack, The Legal Aid Society’s policy director for criminal law reform, laced into the Mamdani administration after being informed of the existing policy. "It is deeply troubling that City Hall has the authority to stop SRG deployments, yet continues to approve them at demonstrations, including at the protests outside the United Nations last week where the mayor himself acknowledged that the deployment was an inappropriate use of police resources,” said Jack, whose group has long advocated for abolishing the SRG. “This further confirms that regulating SRG deployments isn’t the solution. City Hall must finally make good on Mayor Mamdani’s campaign promise to disband SRG for good." The future of the SRG is one of several sources of friction between Mamdani and Jessica Tisch, his politically moderate NYPD commissioner. It’s also an issue that the mayor risks disillusioning his leftist base with the longer he keeps dragging his feet on fulfilling his 2025 campaign pledge. Tisch has defended using the unit, saying it’s a key tool in the department’s network of crime-fighting strategies. But Mamdani — a democratic socialist who, before launching his 2025 mayoral bid, supported calls to defund the NYPD — has long said the unit should be dismantled. Since taking office, he’s said he’s in active conversations with Tisch about finding a way to break up the unit, but those talks haven’t resulted in any tangible action nine months into his term. Founded in 2015, the SRG was initially just tasked with counterterrorism work. The group’s responsibilities have since come to include responding to protests that turn chaotic or violent. In arguing for abolishing the unit, Mamdani and other police reform advocates have pointed to SRG officers racking up disproportionately high rates of misconduct claims while responding to protests. The SRG was subject to a court settlement in 2023 that put new guardrails around how the unit could be deployed during protests. But Mamdani and like-minded voices have contended that’s not enough and that the SRG should be broken up so it can return squarely to its original counterterrorism function. In his remarks on Monday, Mamdani reaffirmed that view. “I have made that promise, I will fulfill that promise,” he said. “The only question is the timeline of it.” — Chris Sommerfeldt  MARK YOUR CALENDAR: Join POLITICO’s New York Outlook: Affordability, Industry & The Economy on Oct. 14 for live conversations about the business and policy decisions being made today — from City Hall to the State Capitol — that will shape the city’s economic future. The lineup includes New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, New York City Economic Development Corp. CEO Anthony Shorris, Partnership for NYC CEO Steven Fulop, Citizens Budget Commission President Andrew Rein, Charles H. Revson Foundation President Maria Torres-Springer, and more. Register now to attend in person or watch the livestream . From the Capitol CORNELL UNDER FIRE: Gov. Kathy Hochul is calling for an independent review of Cornell University’s response to a 2024 gang rape case, as the case draws national attention and the school faces mounting criticism. The Tompkins County district attorney said his office is reopening a criminal probe into an alleged gang rape at a Cornell fraternity house, following a civil lawsuit filed by the plaintiff in mid-September. The plaintiff, a former Cornell student referred to as Jane Doe, alleges in the lawsuit that several men raped her at the Chi Phi house after she was coerced into consuming drugs. The lawsuit names Cornell, several Chi Phi organizations, the former president of Cornell’s Chi Phi chapter, a local bar and unnamed individuals as defendants. The governor called for outside counsel to conduct a “transparent, independent” review of the university’s response to determine whether Cornell “met every obligation to protect its students and pursue justice.” “I support the district attorney’s decision to reopen the criminal investigation,” she said in a statement. “But there are also serious questions about Cornell’s campus culture and its systems for prevention, reporting, and response.” She called the allegations in the case “nothing short of horrifying.” “For any student to come forward after an experience like this takes extraordinary courage,” Hochul said. “No student should ever be left wondering whether the institutions meant to protect them will listen and act.” Rebecca Valli, a Cornell spokesperson, told Playbook the school plans to work with the governor and other state officials. “Cornell shares Governor Hochul’s commitment to addressing campus culture issues, which affect universities across the nation and New York,” Valli said in a statement. “We are committed to continuing to work with state officials to advance student safety and wellbeing.” — Madina Touré EYES ON AI: When it comes to who’s getting involved in addressing the rapid rise of artificial intelligence, Hochul offered a straightforward perspective today: the more the merrier. Speaking to reporters after a meeting of her FutureWorks Commission , which is set to deliver recommendations by the end of the year regarding AI and the workforce, Hochul welcomed the City Council’s recently announced moves to regulate AI . “This is an area where we need an all-hands-on-deck approach,” she said in response to a question regarding whether the Council’s proposals might overlap with the state’s. “I applaud the City Council for getting more information. … If they come up with an idea that would make sense at the state level, we'll embrace it. We have an idea at the state level, it already covers the city. So this is an area, we're on the same team in terms of making sure we get this right, because the risks are too high.” Hochul said the commission is looking to address how AI is reshaping jobs, the best ways to train workers on the technology, protecting those vulnerable to job cuts and “the best ways to harness the benefits of AI for everyday New Yorkers.” Tom Perez, the co-chair of the commission and former U.S. secretary of labor, said there are “more questions than answers at this point” but he has “great optimism that we can tackle this challenge.” — Madison Fernandez FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL SUPER PAC SURGE: Super PACs backing Hochul have reported $4.8 million in contributions since yesterday, giving the governor a comfortable advantage over Republican Bruce Blakeman in the outside spending arms race. Greater Empire State, a committee run by the Democratic Governors Association, received $1 million from the Greater New York Hospital Association – a perennial top spender in New York politics that gave the state Democratic Committee $1.5 million in June. The DGA group also received $500,000 from former gas company CEO John Hess. It reported a dozen four- or five-figure donations from pediatricians and other healthcare groups as well. At least 10 of those have connections to the physician network Somos Community Care, a longtime Hochul benefactor . Additionally, the landlord-backed New York Apartment Association gave $3 million to Leadership for New York, a pro-Hochul super PAC launched by former NYAA official Jay Martin. That committee subsequently transferred $1 million of its money to the one run by DGA. — Bill Mahoney BROOKLYN BATTLE: The state Supreme Court’s appellate division ruled in favor of a group of self-described reformers who were looking to unseat Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn as chair of the Brooklyn Democratic Party. The decision comes just hours before the executive committee is scheduled to meet to vote on the next party chair. Julio Peña III, the district leader put forth by reformers to unseat Bichotte Hermelyn, has been locked in a legal battle over Bichotte Hermelyn’s move to change the makeup of the executive committee — a maneuver she claimed would promote inclusivity, but one her opponents insisted was only carried out to pad her support before the leadership election. A state Supreme Court judge ruled that the vote on the expansion was invalid, but Bichotte Hermelyn appealed the decision. Today’s appellate division ruling voids the expansion — seemingly a win for Peña, who has said he has enough support to win the leadership election under the unchanged structure. But there’s still plenty up in the air. Last night, Bichotte Hermelyn said she decided not to run for another term as chair. After her announcement, City & State reported that she is backing state Assemblymember Nikki Lucas, who had not been actively running for the position. Reformers are in court today looking to prevent this evening’s meeting from happening in light of last week’s chaotic organizational meeting . — Madison Fernandez FROM CITY HALL COMBAT READY: Mamdani released a highly anticipated blueprint to combat rising antisemitism today amid ongoing criticisms that he’s fueled the problem. Under his plan, the Mayor’s Office to Combat Antisemitism will weigh in on $26 million that was allocated in this year’s budget to the Mayor’s Office for the Prevention of Hate Crimes, which has a broader mandate to fight all forms of hate. The cash infusion will mean more money for organizations already engaged in combating antisemitism online and for supporting victims of antisemitic incidents. In particular, the city has doubled the investment in groups doing this work to $6.4 million and has earmarked $1 million for physical security at sensitive sites like synagogues. And it will work to increase visits to the Museum of Jewish Heritage for middle schoolers. “We hold a responsibility to sustain and protect our Jewish neighbors — a responsibility that belongs to each of us,” Mamdani said in a video message accompanying the report. “That is the work we are undertaking at City Hall, and I am asking every New Yorker to join us.” While the report generated plaudits from across the political spectrum, several prominent Jewish organizations said the mayor failed to define antisemitism and to acknowledge that some of his own rhetoric is to blame. “While the Mayor's plan has a number of positive elements, including some increased security funding for Jewish institutions and expanding proven programs, it fails to address a central issue that the Mayor himself has perpetuated: rhetoric that demonizes and delegitimizes Israel inevitably leads to the targeting of Jewish New Yorkers,” the UJA-Federation of New York, JCRC-NY, AJC New York and New York Board of Rabbis wrote in a joint statement. Read more from POLITICO’s Joe Anuta here.  BRIDGE TO HOME: NYC Health + Hospitals is opening a second site for the "Bridge to Home" program, an initiative by former Mayor Eric Adams to provide a place for homeless patients to continue healing after a hospital stay. Patients will be able to stay as long as 12 months at the new Crown Heights site in Brooklyn, where they will have 24/7 medical support from Woodhull Hospital providers and get help applying for permanent housing. "Bridge to Home is a bridge between getting well in the hospital and building a life in the community,” Omar Fattal, NYC Health + Hospitals’ chief behavioral health officer, said during a press conference this afternoon. “And for someone like me who spent many years working in inpatient psychiatry, it means that when we ask, 'Where does this person go next?', we finally have a better answer.” Since the first "Bridge to Home" site opened in Midtown Manhattan in September 2025, 18 participants have moved into permanent housing, according to NYC Health + Hospitals. The first resident of the Crown Heights site, which has capacity for roughly 50 program participants, moves in next week. — Maya Kaufman IN OTHER NEWS INFLUENCER ARMY: A group of influencers under instruction from City Hall are reportedly planning a campaign against top New York CEOs, a claim Mamdani’s administration denies. ( New York Post ) ENERGY FUTURE: A flurry of new energy-intensive projects are underway in upstate New York. ( Times Union ) FRUIT FUMES: Bureaucracy and politics have led to the unraveling of a years-in-the-works plan to modernize a diesel-spewing produce market in the South Bronx. articles.body: A slate of Democrats are running for Congress leaning on their Christian bona fides. Republicans are trying to portray them as wolves in sheep’s clothing. In Texas, Republicans are running ads blasting seminarian James Talarico for saying he’s “a Christian who hates Christianity.” In Iowa, they are going after a pair of clergy in key House races as “PINOS” — “pastors in name only,” because they “don’t profess the true gospel of Jesus Christ.” In Kansas, Republicans pan megachurch pastor Adam Hamilton as “too woke and too weak.” “His sermons are essentially a carbon copy of the Democrat National Committee platform,” said Brent Robertson, chief of staff to Hamilton’s opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kan.), pointing to a past sermon in which Hamilton urged followers to reduce their carbon footprint . The closing arguments on these Democrats — as evidenced by the most recent ads — shows a concerted effort to turn their preaching against them to paint them as fake, corrupt or even blasphemous . In Texas, MAGA Inc. is on air painting Talarico as a “liberal weirdo,” clipping Talarico’s controversial statements, like “Jesus Christ Himself was a radical feminist” and “God is non-binary.” The Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC is on air in Iowa’s 2nd District hitting Presbyterian minister and Democrat Lindsay James as inauthentic: “When the cameras are on, Lindsay James goes into a character, a caring pastor who says what you want to hear, but when there's no spotlight, Lindsay James shows just how radical she can be.” And in Kansas, GOP Sen. Roger Marshall’s campaign is on air slamming Hamilton as a “slimy,” “millionaire megachurch CEO,” saying he “used faith to fatten his wallet” and “asked churchgoers to pony up for God, then use church resources for his own campaign.” “The swamp's got enough money changers,” the ad says. The attacks are coming precisely because these candidates have proven to be formidable candidates in purple to red areas, using their faith backgrounds to bolster themselves against GOP accusations that they’re out of their state’s mainstream. Talarico poses Democrats’ best chance to flip a Texas Senate seat in nearly four decades. Hamilton has turned deep-red Kansas into a battleground. And James and Sarah Trone Garriott, a Lutheran minister, are running tough in a pair of Iowa districts Trump won in 2024. Voters “understand and appreciate authenticity, and they know that faith without works is dead,” said Chaz Molder, the Democratic nominee in Tennessee’s deep-red 2nd District who leads a Sunday School class with his wife. “And just posting scripture on Sunday morning to point out that they went to church is not enough.” But with Democrats’ clerical credibility comes a practical challenge: years and years of on-camera sermons, a treasure trove for oppo researchers. It’s become a challenge in Hamilton’s race, where Vice President JD Vance joined the pile-on earlier this month: During a visit to Iowa, he took a shot at Hamilton as having “kind of a ‘gee whiz, I'm a nice pastor’ vibe,” but said he “tells his congregation not about the gospel of Jesus Christ, but that they need to repent for their white privilege while eating beef.” Democrats have largely brushed off the attacks. Talarico has said he’s “missed the mark” on some of his “cringey” past comments but has doubled down on his sermonizing: “When I take on the politicians who are serving themselves and not the people, I’m doing it on biblical grounds,” he said in a sermon last weekend. A James spokesperson criticized Republicans for “desperately attacking Lindsay’s deeply held faith commitments. If it wasn’t so insulting to other Iowa Christians, it would be laughable.” Hamilton has seen clergy run to his side: 120 fellow Methodist ministers across Kansas wrote an open letter to Marshall telling him to stop attacking Hamilton’s pastoral ministry, saying the attacks “tear at the fabric that is the body of Christ.” “We're not the first Christians to be attacked for our faith, and we won't let smears and lies from a couple of Washington politicians stop us from living out our values in the world,” Hamilton said in a video after Vance’s speech. In many ways, this election marks something of a faith resurgence for the Democratic Party. While only half of Democrat- and Democrat-leaning U.S. adults identify as Christian (a 24-percentage-point decline since 2007), Democrats this cycle are running clergy, Sunday School teachers, chaplains and other devout Christians across the map. “As a person of faith, I think that it's time for the Democratic Party to reassert that Democrats are a big tent, and we have many elected officials from different faiths for whom faith is something very important to them,” said Ben McAdams, the Democratic nominee in Utah’s 1st District and a volunteer Sunday School teacher in his Latter-day Saint congregation in Salt Lake City. “The Republican Party of Donald Trump does not seem to be reflecting the Christian values that I grew up with.” Doug Pagitt, executive director of progressive group Vote Common Good, counts nine clergy running for federal office this cycle as Democrats — something he hasn’t seen before. “The idea that a faith leader, especially a white faith leader, would run as a Democrat and be forthright about it … it's really unusual,” Pagitt said. “We've had candidates [in the past] whose moms were pastors, and they were nervous about mentioning that in the Democratic Party circles. But that seems to have shifted and changed.”
articles.headline: Democrats are running pastors for office. Republicans are attacking their religious comments.

articles.body: CITY HAL 9000: Amid a mad dash to try to regulate artificial intelligence, City Council Speaker Julie Menin is looking to make her mark. The Manhattan lawmaker is planning to hold a hearing with all 51 members of the legislative body next week, and today confirmed the attendance of four major AI firms to discuss both the dangers the technology poses and a suite of Council bills that seek to protect New Yorkers. “Leading experts and AI executives themselves are warning about the potentially grave risks of rapidly advancing AI, and governments have a responsibility to act,” Menin said in a statement announcing she issued a subpoena to SpaceXAI, the artificial intelligence company owned by Elon Musk, to compel the firm to attend. Council hearings — even those run by lesser-known committees — are not known as concise affairs. And the notion of having all 51 members in the room to pepper AI executives with questions can only mean a marathon day with plenty of news coverage. (Remember Randy Mastro’s general counsel nomination hearing in 2024? No? You didn’t tune in for all 11 hours ?) Between the White House’s opposition to any type of AI regulation and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s desire for federal guardrails — though he has enacted an AI ban in elementary schools — a lane has opened for Menin to have her say in what has become one of the defining debates of the political moment. Her muscular posture — her office dangled the possibility of subpoenas in front of the companies she sought for Monday’s hearing — shows she is not going to let it go to waste. The package of bills being pursued by the Council includes a “kill switch” requirement and a new private right of action that would make it easier to sue AI companies. Menin is hoping to get input on that package Monday from artificial intelligence purveyors who agree that something needs to be done to slow the development of frontier AI models. Google, which plans to be there Monday along with Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, has released a white paper calling for a regulatory body that could develop safety standards along with audits for frontier AI models that are pushing the bounds of the technology. Separately, the firm has called for a regulatory framework for AI models like chatbots, which are already being used widely by the general public, and for the government to mitigate disruptions to the economy and workforce. None of the firms have weighed in formally on the Council’s AI package, but one person with knowledge of the bills said there are early questions about how a “kill switch” activated in New York would affect a company’s services elsewhere around the globe, how the private right of action might interact with existing tort laws and whether there are downsides to retaining AI chat histories with consumers for extended periods of time. Separately, there’s also the question of how the city’s AI bills would mesh with a separate AI regulation framework being pursued by Gov. Kathy Hochul. — Joe Anuta From the Capitol GATEWAY DREAMS: The long-awaited Gateway project reached a new milestone today: the start of tunnel boring under the Hudson River. Hochul gathered with officials from New York and New Jersey to celebrate the latest stage of the development — which comes after more than a decade of planning and almost three years of construction work. Following the “ceremonial launch” this morning, two hard-rock tunnel boring machines will be deployed this fall to construct a new rail tunnel between New Jersey and New York Penn Station. The machines are anticipated to clear about 30 feet of earth per day. “We fought and beat efforts from the Trump administration to halt the Gateway project and today, that dream becomes a reality, with state of the art machinery operated by expert union workers starting their journey through soil and bedrock under the Hudson to Penn Station,” Hochul said in a statement. “This is a historic day for New York and a clear demonstration of our ambitions to once again be a state that dreams and builds big.” Construction on Gateway began in late 2023, but the project previously faced a near-shutdown and temporary work stoppages after the Trump administration froze federal funds for it. The project resumed following legal action from New York and New Jersey. — Janaki Chadha DON’T TRUST THE FILINGS: The state Democratic Committee is preemptively casting doubt on the accuracy of a disclosure report due to be filed by Republican opponent Bruce Blakeman on Friday. If the past is any guide, the report won’t contain the definitive list of his financial activity. The campaign finance filing Blakeman submitted on July 15, for example, has since been amended on July 22, Aug. 13, Aug. 25 and Sept. 14. As a result, a significantly different financial picture has formed compared to what was widely reported a couple months ago: Blakeman initially identified $3 million worth of contributions and $1.8 million in expenses over the spring; the latest amended version shows $4.5 million in contributions and $5 million in expenses. The total number of transactions disclosed went from 25,534 to 41,724. Blakeman similarly resubmitted his March disclosure report four times and his January filing thrice. “Either Blakeman wants to trick the press into reporting an inaccurate state of the race, or this guy sucks at math,” state Democratic Committee spokesperson Addison Dick said. The Nassau County executive’s campaign did not respond to a request for comment. — Bill Mahoney FROM CITY HALL ‘NOT IN AN INSHALLAH TIMELINE’: Mamdani said today he’ll release a plan “soon” for disbanding the controversial NYPD unit he pledged to get rid of last year as a candidate — and he’s leaving god out of it. “I will fulfill that promise. The only question is the timeline of it … It'll be not in an inshallah timeline, but an actual one,” he told reporters at a press conference in Manhattan, using the Arabic phrase for godwilling. “The critical point of it is just how to ensure we're doing so while protecting New Yorkers' rights and keeping New Yorkers safe, and that's something that we're going to share more information about soon." Mamdani made the comments after Playbook asked what’s causing the holdup on breaking up the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group, especially in light of the unit being deployed Thursday to arrest activists , including politicians close with the mayor, protesting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. As a candidate last year, Mamdani was adamant that he would, if elected, abolish the SRG over concerns about its heavy-handed responses to protests. But since taking office in January, the mayor has dragged his feet on the pledge. When asked about the status of it, he’s typically just said he’s continuing conversations with NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch — making today’s comments stand out. A spokesperson for the NYPD declined to comment on Mamdani’s remarks. But the spokesperson did note that video posted to social media showed the SRG officers who effected arrests at last week’s anti-Netanyahu demonstrations acted peacefully and were joined by NYPD Community Affairs personnel who informed protesters they would be detained. A political moderate, Tisch has defended using the SRG, once even cracking a joke that seemed aimed at highlighting the static between her and the mayor on the topic. The fate of the SRG is among a number of issues Tisch and Mamdani have clashed on. They also hold divergent views on the issue of the NYPD’s gang database, with Mamdani promising last year to abolish it while Tisch calls it a critical tool that her department uses “every day.” — Chris Sommerfeldt FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL FIRST IN PLAYBOOK: Hochul picked up an endorsement today from Planned Parenthood’s PAC in her bid for a second term. In receiving the endorsement, Hochul touted her work in declaring the state as a “safe haven” for reproductive health care, creating a first-in-the nation paid prenatal leave program and increasing the child tax credit. Planned Parenthood Empire State Votes PAC Chair Robin Chappelle Golston said that the governor "understands what is at stake during relentless federal attacks.” The group also backed Hochul, the first female governor of New York, when she ran for a full term in 2022. Hochul’s opponent, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, has described himself as a “ pro-choice Republican .” — Madison Fernandez IN OTHER NEWS — ZOHRAN’S SHADOW: Hochul is counting on Mamdani to stump for her reelection campaign, but the governor’s advisers are still figuring out the best way for him to do that. ( The New York Times ) — SEX ED: A new study from the New York Civil Liberties Union found that many school districts have selected an abstinence-only sex education curriculum. ( Times Union ) — JOB HUNT: As New York City government continues to reel from staff vacancies, Mamdani is opening a walk-in municipal jobs center to speed up hiring. ( amNewYork ) Missed this morning’s New York Playbook? We forgive you. Read it here .

articles.body: <p>Khadija y Saber cruzan la frontera marroquí a la misma hora, pero no se ven. Ella entra a Ceuta, él va a Marruecos. Vuelve, en realidad. A los dos les impulsa lo mismo: la lluvia. “Me puse de límite el miércoles. Si no encontraba plaza en un centro de menores, me iría, pero mañana va a empezar a llover y no puedo dormir más en la calle”, dice Saber. Cumplió 17 años en agosto, en la playa del Trampolín. Por entonces aún tenía más o menos intacto el sueño que le hizo cruzar el mar, creía que solo era cuestión de aguantar un poco más. Hace días decidió que si no lo había logrado a los dos meses, volvería a Castillejos. Al final no ha sido a los 60 días, sino a los 58. Saber enfila la recta hacia el puesto fronterizo de El Tarajal, y mira su móvil, pero no atrás. “¿Triste? No, estoy cansado. Pero volveré a intentarlo", dice. Desaparece por la frontera con una mochila ligera, donde firmará el retorno voluntario, como las más de 7.000 personas que según las cifras oficiales han emprendido el camino de vuelta por su propio pie. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/ceuta-dos-meses-despues-una-ciudad-paralizada-entre-la-expulsion-y-el-retorno-de-los-migrantes.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/KH6CKK7UQJEY5E2KAJKVTRZ5LU.jpg?auth=06d7dc8bc48e587dc4f557cf99d02b81a6fd10d7ba1a263d0544dc23f1b242d4" width="7008" height="4672" alt="Tras las lluvias de la noche y de la mañana, un joven migrante marroquí sentado frente a su tienda improvisada en la playa del Trampolín en Ceuta, España, el 27 de septiembre."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/BL72PQXIARHPNF57RBIR4IBP6Y.jpg?auth=efca8743ffb9b9c2dc7acea781e3df7c7e58694f036124873d6f48bf05b794f7" width="4240" height="2832" alt="Jóvenes migrantes marroquíes mantienen una conversación con otro compañero desde el tejado de un edificio dentro del polígono industrial cercano a El Tarajal, en Ceuta, España, el 27 de septiembre."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/BH2QTD6SVRFHJG7TORQ3YDKLAA.jpg?auth=add8a29a3dbf50a18d03f0bea9485325ed67808e3b48fa3dab11886c12daabad" width="3876" height="2589" alt="Un joven se arropa con una manta tras pasar la noche mojado debido a las filtraciones de la lluvia en su chabola, situada en un polígono industrial cercano a la frontera de El Tarajal en Ceuta, España, el 27 de septiembre."></img>

"></img><p>De <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2023-03-06/el-pisito.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2023-03-06/el-pisito.html"><i>El pisito, </i>de Rafael Azcona,</a> donde un joven se casa con una anciana para así heredar el piso de ella y poderse algún día instalar allí con su novia, hasta <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-23/maricarmen-se-queda-un-centenar-de-activistas-espera-junto-a-la-anciana-a-la-comision-judicial.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-23/maricarmen-se-queda-un-centenar-de-activistas-espera-junto-a-la-anciana-a-la-comision-judicial.html">el desahucio de Maricarmen</a>, perpetrado la semana pasada, se condensa la historia inmobiliaria de Madrid como género literario. Esta fue la aventura de nuestros padres y será la aventura de nuestros hijos: sobrevivir con dignidad a un entorno social áspero y desalmado. Las grandes ciudades son máquinas de fabricar soledades acompañadas. La otra mañana, la falta de imaginación moral de las sentencias de la Audiencia Provincial y del Supremo <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-23/el-simbolo-de-un-derecho-roto.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-23/el-simbolo-de-un-derecho-roto.html">permitió arrancar de su casa</a> a una mujer de 87 años y sacarla de allí en camilla tras toda una vida entre esas paredes. Hizo falta sumar varias dotaciones de antidisturbios, equipo médico de urgencia, helicópteros y <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/tirones-de-cuello-porrazos-y-aranazos-las-agresiones-policiales-del-desahucio-de-maricarmen-que-investigara-delegacion-de-gobierno.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-25/tirones-de-cuello-porrazos-y-aranazos-las-agresiones-policiales-del-desahucio-de-maricarmen-que-investigara-delegacion-de-gobierno.html">brutales cargas contra la resistencia civil</a> como si se afrontara la amenaza de un comando terrorista. El terrorismo inmobiliario tiene de su parte a la ley, mientras no se racionalice la legislación. La precariedad histórica en los últimos años ha aumentado con la venta de pisos de protección oficial <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-09-28/las-leyes-que-dieron-alas-a-los-buitres.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-09-28/las-leyes-que-dieron-alas-a-los-buitres.html">a los fondos de capital</a> y la festiva llegada de las grandes fortunas que, con el dinero extraído de sus naciones empobrecidas, compran a precios desorbitados los mejores espacios de la capital. A esto lo llamamos éxito. Imagínense lo que será el fracaso.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-29/terror-inmobiliario.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Terror inmobiliario

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/H6ETR6DFKBCKBKEK5AGQBQW3O4.jpg?auth=eadf10c8843292a528c4ae2aa499604784373c2e12979946cf8cbd2bda60c766" width="8192" height="5464" alt="La acampada de Sol, este lunes. "></img><p>Ana Orantes Ruiz <a href="https://elpais.com/sociedad/2022-12-17/25-anos-del-asesinato-de-ana-orantes-que-cambio-la-lucha-contra-la-violencia-machista-en-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/sociedad/2022-12-17/25-anos-del-asesinato-de-ana-orantes-que-cambio-la-lucha-contra-la-violencia-machista-en-espana.html">murió asesinada por su exmarido</a> el 17 de diciembre de 1997. Dos semanas antes, había aparecido en un programa de Canal Sur contando 40 años de palizas. Se había divorciado, pero el juez determinó que ella y su marido siguieran en su casa de Cúllar Vega (Granada). Ella arriba, él abajo, compartiendo el patio. Él pasaba poco por allí, pero a veces volvía. La última, después de verla en la tele. <a href="https://elpais.com/diario/1997/12/18/espana/882399613_850215.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/diario/1997/12/18/espana/882399613_850215.html">La quemó viva en aquel patio compartido.</a> Fue una más de las mujeres maltratadas por sus parejas. De las mujeres asesinadas. Pero su historia conmocionó a la sociedad y <a href="https://elpais.com/politica/2017/11/24/actualidad/1511548723_149638.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/politica/2017/11/24/actualidad/1511548723_149638.html">convirtió en público un problema</a> que hasta entonces se consideraba privado. Este crimen cambió la sensibilidad de la sociedad e impulsó cambios legislativos para afrontarla. En 1999, el Gobierno de Aznar modificó el Código Penal. La violencia psicológica se convirtió en delito y aparecieron las órdenes de alejamiento. En 2004, el Gobierno de Zapatero aprobó <a href="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-21760" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2004-21760">la ley integral contra la violencia de género</a> y en 2007, <a href="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6115" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2007-6115">la Ley para la Igualdad Efectiva de Mujeres y Hombres.</a> El crimen de Ana Orantes despertó la conciencia colectiva ante un problema social que ya existía. Y ese despertar cambió un marco legal que hasta entonces no contemplaba respuestas.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-29/maricarmen-una-mas-de-las-que-impulsaron-un-cambio.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Aún no había amanecido cuando los agentes antidisturbios bajaron a la arena de Benítez. En el último tramo de la playa, ubicada a pocos metros de El Trampolín, permanecían aún unas 400 personas de origen magrebí —casi todos hombres— <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-28/el-delegado-de-ceuta-solicito-al-gobierno-refuerzos-ante-el-agravamiento-de-la-presion-migratoria-una-semana-antes-de-la-avalancha.html?mrfhud=true" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-28/el-delegado-de-ceuta-solicito-al-gobierno-refuerzos-ante-el-agravamiento-de-la-presion-migratoria-una-semana-antes-de-la-avalancha.html?mrfhud=true">que entraron en Ceuta con el cruce masivo</a> y que malvivían en tiendas improvisadas. Buena parte de este asentamiento fue desalojado ya el domingo, pero todavía quedaban decenas de cabañas que finalmente han sido eliminadas mediante un segundo operativo celebrado este martes. A las ocho de la mañana, los policías empezaron a exigir a los migrantes que abandonaran las tiendas. “¡Todo el mundo fuera!”, gritaba una agente. Dentro de los cobertizos los migrantes despertaban del sueño nocturno y salían con sus enseres. “¿A Marruecos?, ¿a Marruecos?”, preguntaban una y otra vez ante el temor a ser deportados. Luego fueron trasladados en distintos autobuses con rumbo al Centro de Atención Temporal de Extranjeros (CATE) situado en el paso de El Tarajal, pero cerca de dos centenares acabaron volviendo de regreso al reino alauí. En el otro lado del paso fronterizo, gendarmes marroquíes los montaban en otros vehículos y los llevaban hasta distintos puntos del país vecino.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/el-gobierno-impulsa-el-retorno-voluntario-de-decenas-de-migrantes-a-marruecos-con-el-desalojo-de-las-playas-de-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/IBF56EBPVFC7ZGGRG3WTO3OLJM.jpeg?auth=fe8d76248c1be23bcfcba3a67626faed63060f420a531cbb9ade89366196752b" width="661" height="367" alt="Un migrante vuelve "voluntariamente", en el paso de El Tarajal, este martes."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/VHLFG4JDYJEV3HIFJHC2JFPPDQ.jpg?auth=7f43c5282ebc813470e8bb019f664d5376b664cbb1a11e1d96ae82170f0e00dc" width="4240" height="2832" alt="Policías antidisturbios se despliegan durante el operativo de desalojo en playa de Benítez."></img>
articles.headline: El Gobierno impulsa el “retorno voluntario” de decenas de migrantes a Marruecos con el desalojo de las playas de Ceuta

articles.body: <p>No resulta fácil entender por qué ha sido tan complicado que una ley aprobada por el Parlamento y <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-22/el-constitucional-devuelve-la-ponencia-que-se-opone-a-amnistiar-la-malversacion-a-los-lideres-del-proces.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-22/el-constitucional-devuelve-la-ponencia-que-se-opone-a-amnistiar-la-malversacion-a-los-lideres-del-proces.html">avalada por el Constitucional</a> haya tardado más de dos años en poder aplicarse plenamente. No es razonable que en un país democrático ocurra algo así, que es lo que ha sucedido con la ley de amnistía. Sin duda hay factores políticos que han incidido en este retraso, pero lamentablemente también otros más relacionados con la contaminación que en las dos últimas legislaturas ha contagiado las más diversas sedes judiciales. Resulta curioso que algunos de los que más han reivindicado la defensa del Estado de derecho menos hayan respetado sus reglas, incluido el llamamiento a que “quien pueda hacer, que haga”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/el-constitucional-cierra-el-circulo-sobre-la-amnistia.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, ha enarbolado este martes, ante un nutrido grupo de estudiantes en Madrid, un alegato de regusto europeo contra la “desesperanza”. articles.body: <p>La Puerta del Sol, en Madrid, se ha ido llenando de manifestantes desde que el sábado el Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos convocara a una <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-29/radiografia-de-la-acampada-de-sol-asi-se-organizo-en-una-noche-el-campamento-que-ya-reune-a-miles.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-29/radiografia-de-la-acampada-de-sol-asi-se-organizo-en-una-noche-el-campamento-que-ya-reune-a-miles.html">acampada para defender el derecho a la vivienda</a>, tras la manifestación en apoyo a María del Carmen Abascal, <i>Maricarmen</i>, la vecina de 87 años del madrileño distrito de Retiro que fue desahuciada la pasada semana de la casa en la que vivió durante más de 70 años. Desde las poco más de 100 tiendas que se contaban la noche del sábado hasta las aproximadamente 300 que hay este martes; desde los primeros 800 manifestantes hasta los varios miles que se registran este martes. La imagen de la céntrica plaza madrileña repleta de manifestantes tras cuatro días de protestas no ha sido común en los últimos años y recuerda, indudablemente, a la que dejaron las cerca de 15.000 personas que se llegaron a reunir en ese mismo lugar hace 15 años tras el 15-M. Uno de los integrantes del Sindicato ha explicado que la organización, en realidad, ya no lidera la acampada: “La acampada es una entidad propia, ha crecido tanto…”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2026-09-29/miles-de-manifestantes-se-unen-en-sol-para-defender-la-vivienda-la-acampada-es-una-entidad-propia.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Miles de manifestantes se unen en Sol para defender la vivienda: “La acampada es una entidad propia”

articles.body: <p>La sacudida del desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal ha impulsado este martes la aprobación en el Consejo de Ministros de <a href="https://elpais.com/economia/vivienda/2026-09-29/las-medidas-de-vivienda-del-acuerdo-ampliacion-hasta-2030-de-la-proteccion-frente-a-los-desahucios-y-prorroga-dos-anos-de-los-alquileres.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/economia/vivienda/2026-09-29/las-medidas-de-vivienda-del-acuerdo-ampliacion-hasta-2030-de-la-proteccion-frente-a-los-desahucios-y-prorroga-dos-anos-de-los-alquileres.html">una batería de medidas sobre vivienda a través de dos reales decretos ley</a> que se someterán a votación en un Pleno extraordinario en el Congreso este mismo viernes. Pedro Sánchez confía en aprovechar así la oleada de indignación por el desalojo de la anciana de 87 años para recomponer el maltrecho bloque de la investidura y lograr la cuadratura del círculo que durante meses ha sido imposible por los vetos cruzados entre Junts y Podemos. Una victoria en las Cortes le permitiría recuperar la iniciativa justo cuando se cumplen dos meses de la crisis de Ceuta, donde la reacción tardía a la crisis fronteriza le ha supuesto al presidente un gran desgaste. “El desahucio de Maricarmen ha sido un fracaso colectivo pero el Congreso tiene una oportunidad única para decirle que su sufrimiento ha merecido la pena y que va a servir para que no lo vivan otras personas”, ha recalcado Isabel Rodríguez, la ministra de vivienda, que ha apelado a la “altura de miras” y “responsabilidad” de los socios de la investidura para convalidar el paquete de medidas dentro de menos de 72 horas. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-29/el-gobierno-aprueba-la-proteccion-frente-a-los-desahucios-hasta-2030-y-la-prorroga-de-los-contratos-de-alquiler-hasta-2028.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

A menys de 140 quilòmetres de casa tens volcans, mines de sal, cales amagades, aus rapinyaires en llibertat i llacs on practicar rem. A l’agenda de betevé sabem que n’hi ha moltes més, però aquí teniu les nostres propostes. Catalunya en Miniatura, a Torrelles de Llobregat Catalunya en Miniatura és un dels parcs temàtics de maquetes més grans del món i el més extens d’Europa. Està situat al municipi de Torrelles de Llobregat , a uns 20 quilòmetres de Barcelona. Diverbosc a Cerdanyola Diverbosc (abans, El Bosc Tancat) és un parc d’aventura en plena natura a Cerdanyola del Vallès . Ofereix circuits entre els arbres i tirolines, tant per a nens com per a adults i quatre grans piscines. A 15 km de Barcelona. articles.body: Cada dia es fan 2,1 milions de desplaçaments entre Barcelona i els municipis de l’entorn, i el vehicle privat hi té un paper destacat. El 41 % dels viatges a la primera corona són en vehicle privat , la xifra s’eleva al 57 % a la resta de la regió metropolitana i al 63 % si són a la resta de la província. L’Ajuntament de Barcelona vol capgirar aquestes xifres i encarregarà estudis dels quatre corredors de connexió de la ciutat per aportar solucions per millorar la mobilitat interurbana , tenint en compte també la transformació de la ciutat, i el context d’emergència climàtica. Aquests corredors o portes d’entrada són l’avinguda Diagonal , l’avinguda Meridiana , la porta Gran Via nord , i la porta Gran Via sud i ronda Litoral sud . També et pot interessar Barcelona posarà ordre a parades de bus interurbà i en crearà de noves per evitar aglomeracions Jaume Planagumà 2 minuts de lectura L’estudi de la Meridiana, en marxa Dels quatre estudis a realitzar, el de Porta Meridiana ja està en fase d’execució, i la resta de concursos s’anunciaran “pròximament”. El consistori vol tenir per primera vegada un “paper central” en les polítiques de mobilitat de les persones i les mercaderies que entren i surten cada dia de la ciutat, més enllà del terme municipal. És a dir, “incidir en la definició i transformació de les connexions interurbanes”. I tot plegat, tenint en compte els grans projectes de transformació que hi ha en marxa i que seran nous focus de mobilitat, com el Campus Clínic a la Diagonal, la Sagrera o el Bioclúster de Bellvitge. La temperatura mitjana provisional és de 24,8 ºC , la més alta registrada en un mes de setembre. És un valor que destaca clarament respecte dels registres anteriors: queda 1,3 ºC per sobre de l’anterior rècord, del 1987 . Com mostra la gràfica, la diferència amb els valors dels altres setembres és especialment notable. El setembre d’enguany no ha fet de pont cap a la tardor, sinó que ha estat una prolongació de l’estiu , amb temperatures elevades també durant les nits. I tot plegat, quan només falten 100 dies per acabar l’any. Les dades mostren fins a quin punt la calor ha dominat el setembre. 27 dels 30 dies del mes han estat per sobre de la temperatura mitjana de referència . Només tres dies —el 9, el 10 i el 17— han quedat per sota, i ho han fet de manera poc destacada: de mitjana, 1,3 ºC per sota del normal . La diferència és molt més notable quan mirem els dies càlids. Els 27 dies amb anomalia positiva han estat, de mitjana, 4,5 ºC per sobre de la mitjana . Els episodis de calor més excepcionals es van concentrar els dies 5 i 15 de setembre. El dia 5 va registrar la temperatura mitjana més alta del mes, 30,45 ºC , mentre que el dia 15 va ser el que es va allunyar més del que és habitual, amb una anomalia de +8,15 ºC, davant dels +7,85 ºC del dia 5. En el conjunt del mes, la temperatura mitjana ha estat de 24,76 ºC, amb una anomalia mitjana de +3,95 ºC respecte de la mitjana de referència . Les dades dibuixen, per tant, un setembre en què la calor no només ha estat persistent, sinó també molt més intensa del que és habitual . articles.body: Dormir al carrer implica, en la immensa majoria dels casos, patir situacions de violència i discriminació . Segons Arrels Fundació , el 83,3 % de les persones que viuen al carrer a Barcelona van ser víctimes d’algun tipus d’agressió durant el 2025: sis de cada 10 van patir insults, amenaces o humiliacions i gairebé la meitat agressions físiques. A més, a una tercera part se’ls van restringir l’accés a establiments. Són les principals conclusions de l’informe sobre victimització i aporofòbia que l’entitat ha elaborat a partir de més de 1.300 enquestes a persones sense llar, que es van fer entre els anys 2023 i 2025. Arrels destaca que les dones tenen percentatges més alts de discriminació que els homes: més d’un 40 % han partir agressions sexuals. Un indicador, que segons Arrels, creix cada vegada més, però que d’altra banda , és difícil de quantificar per la infradenúncia. La majoria de les persones sense llar no ho fan perquè pensen que no servirà de res , o perquè no confien en la policia ni en la justícia . D’altres tenen por a represàlies o no sabien com podien fer-ho. De fet, Arrels calcula que dues de cada tres agressions no es denuncien. Considera que els indicadors generals de delictes d’odi tenen en compte aspectes associats al racisme o l’homofòbia, per exemple, però no al sensellarisme. Reclamen també que es creïn canals de denúncia fora de les comissaries, a través de serveis socials, punts mòbils o entitats. articles.body: El Poble Espanyol torna amb Creepy per celebrar el Halloween 2026 , que atemorirà un any més els visitants. Un espectacle que ofereix la versió diürna, dirigida al públic familiar (versió haunted ) i una altra a partir de la tarda-vespre, més apropiada per a un públic jove i adult (versió scream ) . Hi trobaràs més de 10 espais decorats, més de 35 personatges i un recorregut guiat amb diverses proves i l’entrada a dos túnels del terror. A banda, aquest any també torna els divendres i el mateix 31 d’octubre, La zona , una experiència de terror per a adults, amb més de 4.000 m² de recorregut que els organitzadors van estrenar l’any passat assegurant que seria “un autèntic malson”. Consulta totes les activitats de Halloween al Poble Espanyol . Et detallem les dates, el programa i tots els detalls del Creepy Halloween family i La zona . Recorda que totes dues propostes inclouen l’ entrada al recinte . Ah, i s’hi afegeix la quarta edició de Mascarada el 31 d’octubre. T’ho expliquem tot, aquí. Quan? Creepy Halloween family : els caps de setmana i festius del 17 d’octubre a l’1 de novembre del 2026 , de 10 a 21 h els dissabtes, i de 10 a 20 h els diumenges (menys el 31 d’octubre, de 10 a 19 h). La zona : els divendres 16, 23, 30 i 31 d’octubre del 2026 , a partir de les 20 h i la cua estarà oberta fins les 23.40 h. La Mascarada : 31 d’octubre a la nit. On? Al Poble Espanyol . Preus Creepy Halloween family : des de 12,5 € (sense túnels)i 14,50 (amb túnels) La zona : a partir de 24 € La Mascarada: a partir de 18 € Què hi trobaràs? Creepy Halloween family 17, 18, 24 i 25 i 31 d’octubre i 1 de novembre , de 10 a 17 h i de 17 a 21 h. Preu: de 12,5 a 16,5 €. El Poble Espanyol ensenya la seva cara més fosca en una activitat de por adaptada al públic infantil (a partir dels tres anys). Els visitants hauran de resoldre enigmes i s’endinsaran en dos túnels misteriosos. Hi haurà espectacles de màgia, tallers familiars, actuacions i zona de jocs i podràs conèixer els 35 personatges terroríficament divertits i decoracions impressionants. A més, es podran visitar dos túnels de terror en dues versions: de 10 a 17 h, la versió haunted , amb un nivell més adaptat al públic familiar (a partir dels tres anys); i de 17 a 21 h, la versió scream , amb una mica més d’intensitat (recomanat per a infants a partir de set anys). La zona 16 i 23 d’octubre (a les 20 h) 30 d’octubre (a les 19 h) i 31 d’octubre (a les 20.30 h). Última entrada de 23 a 23.40 h, depèn aforament. Preu a partir de 24 €. Les nits de divendres, des de l’any passat, pots viure al Poble Espanyol una experiència de terror pertorbadora , en què bona part del recinte està a les fosques i es transforma en un escenari terrorífic. La zona inclou més de 4.000 m² de recorregut en què l’adrenalina està garantida: més de 30 personatges faran del passeig un “autèntic malson”. En finalitzar el recorregut, es pot gaudir d’un espai amb música, barra, gastronomia i jocs. Important! L’entrada a aquesta activitat no es fa per l’accés principal del Poble Espanyol, sinó que es fa pel passeig de Jean Forestier. Mascarada I al mateix Poble Espanyol es celebra la quarta edició de la festa Mascarada. Coincidint amb la nit de Halloween, el dissabte 31 d’octubre torna aquesta gran celebració amb els millors èxits de pop, música urbana i electrònica . L’altre tret distintiu d’aquesta festa és el fet que s’anima els assistents a portar una màscara per submergir-se en el concepte de Mascarada . Si accedeixes a la festa abans de la 1 h, l’entrada et dona dret a una consumició. articles.body: El fort episodi de pluja d’aquest dimarts ha colpejat la ciutat amb ganes i, en especial, ha deixat els barris de muntanya molt afectats. La majoria de les incidències són amb camins, pistes i carreteres que s’han quedat impracticables . Un dels punts on s’acumulen centenars de pedres i vegetació arrossegades per la força de l’aigua és a Sant Genís dels Agudells . La pluja ha provocat un despreniment al carrer de Cànoves, 132 i com a conseqüència s’ha tallat el trànsit de vehicles i el Bus del Barri 112 ha desviat el recorregut. També et pot interessar Més de 100 litres a Collserola: balanç de l’episodi de pluja a Barcelona i a l’entorn metropolità Manel Cascante Torrella 2 minuts de lectura Segons els Bombers de Barcelona caldrà una grua per treure tota la runa i la brossa que han caigut, una feina que els veïns de la zona esperen “que comenci aviat perquè la part alta està incomunicada “, apunta a l’ Infobarris Joli Fontoba, del Col·lectiu Ecologista Agudells. A més, asseguren que ja feia temps que alertaven que aquest despreniment amb pluges fortes era molt probable que es produís. “Les terres que tallen la carretera provenen de la benzinera de l’Arrabassada, creiem que cal posar un mur de contenció per reforçar la zona”, diu Fontoba. La runa al carrer de Cànoves, a Sant Genís dels Agudells A Torre Baró, neteja veïnal A la zona nord de la ciutat un altre punt amb moltes afectacions ha estat el barri de Torre Baró . La imatge de la carretera Alta de les Roquetes és la d’un vial totalment col·lapsat de pedres on és impossible circular . Els veïns asseguren que “per culpa dels despreniments de terra no passa el bus 182, que uneix el barri amb Canyelles”. També hi ha altres ubicacions afectades al barri com el carrer de l’Escolapi Càncer i el de Castellfollit, amb despreniments i amb les clavegueres embussades. De fet, per a aquest dimecres al matí han organitzat una trobada per netejar la zona. “ Estem cansats d’estar aïllats i d’esperar, ha arribat el moment d’actuar junts”, expliquen en una convocatòria a les xarxes. Així mateix, fan una crida a portar eines que tinguin per casa els veïns i aconseguir així treure les pedres i reduir els efectes de l’aiguat . Veïns de Torre Baró obren el pas a la rotonda de Manolo Vital Una esllavissada a la plaça del Teix Collserola és un dels punts on es van registrar més litres d’aigua. Concretament, a Can Rectoret el recompte calcula 111 litres per metre quadrat durant la jornada de dimarts. A més, els veïns de la plaça del Teix, al mateix Can Rectoret, han tornat a patir una esllavissada important que ha afectat alguns vehicles que hi havia estacionats a la zona. De fet, no és la primera vegada que passa al barri. Fa set anys, l’abril del 2020, ja en van patir una altra de gran afectació , quan van haver de retirar 42 camions de terra de la plaça i s’hi va haver de tallar el trànsit. articles.body: (ACN) El segon dels nous decrets d’habitatge del Govern espanyol, referent a les mesures per estabilitzar els contractes de lloguer, preveu obligar els propietaris a “indemnitzar” els llogaters si no els renoven els contractes. Segons consta a l’esborrany de la llei, al qual ha tingut accés l’ACN, si arribada la data de venciment del contracte cap de les parts ha notificat la voluntat de no prorrogar-lo, el contracte es renovarà “obligatòriament” per terminis successius de cinc o set anys. Si l’arrendador comunica la voluntat de no prorrogar el contracte, estarà obligat a compensar l’arrendatari amb una quantitat equivalent a l’import de dotze mensualitats de renda d’un habitatge similar. Segons consta al decret, la indemnització no seria procedent quan la no-pròrroga respongui a una causa “justificada”. Aquí es mencionen casos com que l’arrendador, essent persona física, necessiti l’habitatge per a si mateix o per als seus familiars de segon grau, que l’arrendatari no habiti de manera efectiva l’habitatge arrendat o que disposi d’un altre habitatge apte en el mateix municipi. Els partits de l’oposició però ja han fet palesa la seva disconformitat amb aquest decret i han anunciat que el seu vot serà desfavorable . També et pot interessar Publicat al BOE el primer decret d’habitatge: les claus de les mesures per frenar els desnonaments Redacció 2 minuts de lectura “Necessitat real de l’arrendador” La indemnització compleix una “doble funció”. D’una banda, compensa la llar pels costos que suposa l’extinció d’un contracte complert. De l’altra, fa que “la decisió de no prorrogar internalitzi el cost que trasllada a l’altra part”. D’aquesta manera, es busca que no prorrogar un contracte “respongui a una necessitat real de l’arrendador i no a la mera expectativa d’obtenir una renda superior amb un nou arrendatari”, indica l’esborrany. Segons defensa el Govern espanyol en el text, la mesura no restringeix l’oferta d’habitatge de lloguer ni “altera l’equilibri de les prestacions del contracte”. “L’arrendador manté la llibertat de no prorrogar el contracte en cadascun dels seus venciments, amb l’únic deure de compensar l’arrendatari, i continua percebent la renda pactada amb les seves actualitzacions”, remarquen. També et pot interessar Acampada pel dret a l’habitatge a la plaça de Catalunya Arnau Vaqué Guillem González Claramunt Marc Bermejo Sílvia Gutiérrez 2 minuts de lectura França, Alemanya i Països Baixos L’exposició de motius de la norma també recorda que diverses legislacions europees han optat recentment per fórmules per dotar de més estabilitat l’arrendament d’habitatge. “A Alemanya, el contracte és, per regla general, de durada indefinida i l’arrendador només pot posar-hi fi quan acrediti un interès legítim; a França, el contracte es renova tàcitament per períodes de tres anys, o de sis si l’arrendador és una persona jurídica, i la no-renovació per part de l’arrendador exigeix un preavís de sis mesos i una causa taxada; als Països Baixos, la reforma aprovada el 2024 ha restablert el contracte de durada indefinida com a règim ordinari”, apunten. També et pot interessar Illa anuncia que el govern comprarà part de l’habitatge dels majors de 40 anys Redacció 2 minuts de lectura “L’experiència comparada mostra que l’estabilitat del vincle arrendatici no és incompatible amb un mercat de lloguer ampli i dinàmic, sinó una de les seves condicions: redueix la rotació, els períodes de desocupació i els costos de transacció, i permet a les famílies planificar la seva vida sobre una base certa”, conclouen.

articles.body: (Agències/Redacció) El Butlletí Oficial de l’Estat (BOE) ha publicat aquest dimecres el text final d’un dels dos decrets llei d’habitatge anunciats pel Govern espanyol . El text estableix mesures per frenar l’especulació immobiliària, protegir els llogaters i ampliar el parc públic d’habitatges , i també paralitza els desnonaments fins al 31 de desembre del 2030 a totes les persones que no disposin d’una alternativa d’habitatge. També et pot interessar Llum verda als decrets de renovació automàtica dels lloguers i que limiten els desnonaments Redacció 3 minuts de lectura Aquestes són algunes de les claus de l’anomenat decret Maricarmen. Fre als desnonaments i l’especulació Suspensió dels desnonaments fins al 31 de desembre del 2030 : es paralitzen els desnonaments quan les persones no disposin d’una alternativa i l’habitatge sigui d’un fons voltor. Obligació per a les comunitats autònomes : seran les encarregades d’evitar els desnonaments de llogaters que hagin acumulat deutes amb particulars i posteriorment l’Estat les “compensarà”. Segons la norma, i d’acord amb les estadístiques, aquesta regulació serà aplicable “a la immensa majoria dels casos de desnonament”.  Límits a la compra especulativa : es prohibeix fins al 31 de desembre del 2028 l’adquisició d’habitatge per part de fons d’inversió per un preu inferior al 70 % del seu valor de taxació de mercat. En queden exclosos els ens i les entitats del sector públic que tinguin com a finalitat la promoció i gestió d’habitatge social i assequible. Protecció als llogaters i control del frau Pròrroga extraordinària : els contractes vigents per habitatge habitual es podran acollir a una pròrroga extraordinària de fins a dos anys. Límits al lloguer de temporada i d’habitacions : els contractes de lloguer temporal hauran d’acreditar la causa de la temporalitat. En el cas de contractes d’habitacions, la suma dels contractes no podrà superar el preu del lloguer de l’immoble. En el cas de la legislació catalana de lloguer temporal i d’habitacions, s’hi inclou una clàusula per respectar la normativa de les comunitats autònomes. Mesures i incentius fiscals Deduccions al lloguer : es crea una deducció del 10 % per lloguer de l’habitatge habitual. Hi podran accedir els contribuents amb una base imposable inferior a 33.007,20 euros anuals. Desgravació per als propietaris : els qui redueixin el preu dels lloguers podran obtenir rebaixes fiscals en l’IRPF. Recàrrecs als pisos turístics : s’obliga a tributar l’IVA per valor del 10 %, de manera que tributin com un negoci. A més, els ajuntaments poden establir un recàrrec de l’IBI dels pisos turístics i els que es considerin buits. També et pot interessar Els propietaris de pisos rebutgen el decret Maricarmen: “No es poden fer normes d’avui a demà” Lola Santiago 1 minut de lectura El segon decret es publicarà dijous El segon decret d’habitatge, que recull la reforma de les pròrrogues dels lloguers per donar estabilitat als llogaters, es publicarà dijous. Segons aquesta norma, els llogaters tenen estabilitat total i els propietaris hauran d’indemnitzar-los si volen recuperar l’habitatge excepte per una causa de força major. El Congrés dels Diputats ha rebut aquesta nit els dos nous decrets llei d’habitatge i la presidenta de la cambra, Francina Armengol, ha convocat una trobada telemàtica de la Mesa per poder-los qualificar. Està previst que divendres a les 11 del matí se celebri un ple extraordinari demanat pel Govern espanyol per debatre i votar els dos decrets. articles.body: El Sindicat d’Habitatge Socialista de Catalunya considera que els decrets d’habitatge aprovats pel Govern espanyol aquest dimarts al Consell de Ministres “no estan a l’altura de les mobilitzacions”. Això després després de llegir la lletra petita d’un dels dos textos, que s’ha publicat aquest matí al Butlletí Oficial de l’Estat (BOE) . Segons ha explicat la seva portaveu, Pilar Sánchez, al Bon dia, Barcelona , les mesures són insuficients davant de la crisi d’habitatge que s’està vivint i per això demanen polítiques “que vagin més enllà d’aquestes engrunes “. Entre les propostes que posen sobre la taula: abaixar els lloguers a la meitat i expropiar tots els pisos dels fons d’inversió . “No ens podem quedar en un decret farsa “, ha afegit. També et pot interessar Vox vol protecció també per als propietaris: “Si fem la guerra amb qui té pisos, no podrem llogar” Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura Nova protesta aquest dissabte Davant d’aquest escenari, el sindicat ha deixat clar que “la lluita no es pot aturar aquí”. Per això, han convocat una manifestació el proper dissabte, 3 d’octubre , a l’Hospitalet del Llobregat . La protesta començarà a les 19 h a la plaça de Pius XII , tot i que a les 18 h sortirà una gran columna des de la plaça d’Espanya de Barcelona. Tot plegat, per seguir pressionant les administracions i recordar l’Olga, la dona que es va suïcidar després de ser desnonada . “Hem de desbordar l’Hospitalet”, ha conclòs. També et pot interessar Acampada pel dret a l’habitatge a la plaça de Catalunya Arnau Vaqué Guillem González Claramunt Marc Bermejo Sílvia Gutiérrez 2 minuts de lectura Recupera l’entrevista sencera

articles.body: Els treballadors del Port de Barcelona no es rendeixen i tornen a sortir al carrer contra les retallades salarials. Ja ho van fer al juliol i aquest dimecres s’han mobilitzat contra la proposta de l’empresa per regularitzar el que anomena com a “desajust tècnic acumulat en el temps”. La mobilització ha arrencat a quarts de nou del matí al moll de Barcelona, davant de la Torre de Jaume I. Els manifestants, calculen unes 250 persones , han tallat la plaça de les Drassanes i la ronda del Litoral fins a tornar al World Trade Center, on s’ha celebrat el consell d’administració. També et pot interessar Conflicte laboral al Port de Barcelona: què passa i per què protesten els treballadors? Olga Borràs Boada 4 minuts de lectura Una “desviació” en el salari La retallada salarial que es vol aplicar al personal de l’Autoritat Portuària de Barcelona és arran d’un informe de la Intervenció General de l’Administració de l’Estat que va trobar que hi havia una “desviació” en el salari dels treballadors . Es tracta, explica, d’una diferència entre la massa salarial autoritzada i el que es va acabar abonant en determinats conceptes retributius. Per tant, diu el Port, és fruit “d’un desajust tècnic acumulat en el temps” . La proposta que fa el Port per complir aquests ajustos és destinar una part dels increments salarials que pugui aprovar el sector públic a corregir la desviació. La plantilla considera, però, que hi ha altres formes per corregir-la. Interpel·len també el Ministeri de Transports —sota qui es troba Ports de l’Estat, a què pertany el de Barcelona— per tenir “bloquejat” el conveni col·lectiu i el d’Hisenda. Els treballadors insisteixen a demanar al Port que no es precipiti i no doni per vàlid l’informe de la Intervenció General de l’Administració de l’Estat.
